newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on central bank defence.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on central bank defence.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart on Friday after the central bank launched a stout -- and well-timed -- defence amid surging quarter-end demand for the greenback, dealers said.

The slowly depreciating local unit traded at eight-year low levels until the final seconds, when the day's last recorded transactions pushed the rate slightly higher. The Taiwan dollar closed at T$27.913 against Thursday's T$27.920 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$341 million, US$102 million of which came in the last 15 minutes -- when dealers said central bank intervention was strong and conspicuous.
"The central bank basically said enough is enough, no more depreciation for now," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The Taiwan dollar dipped as low as T$27.940 and hovered around T$27.930 for much of the day before rebounding in the final seconds to end at the day's high.
A further depreciation would have pulled the local currency below an eight-year low against the U.S. dollar, which was set on Thursday.
The Taiwan dollar's depreciation toward the psychological T$28 benchmark, which has unfolded gradually since early 1997, has been in line with expectations of senior Taipei dealers.

Of six senior dealers queried in an informal May 30 Reuters Poll, four said the dollar would break support at T$28 in the third quarter due to sluggish economic growth and political uncertainty -- but not before the central bank put up a strong defence to slow the slide.
Two said they expected the central bank to mount such a concerted defence that the slide would stop just short of T$28.
On Friday, dealers said they expected the central bank to act aggressively to keep the local dollar above the T$27.95 support level in the near term.
"The central bank does not mind a downtrend, but it does mind a sharp swing," said another dealer.
A T$27.90-93 range was seen for Saturday's shortened session.
